source.title: Improving generalization of deep neural networks by leveraging margin distribution
source.authors: Shen-Huan Lyu; Lu Wang; Zhi-Hua Zhou

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including its results table and figures.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether dropout and its own margin-distribution loss affect held-out performance, and whether a margin-distribution measure tracks the generalization gap. Its experiments use test accuracy and empirical gap rather than the claim versions’ methods in most cases.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports test accuracy for four losses under dropout and no-dropout conditions across three datasets, two batch-normalization conditions, and two training-set fractions. Rows below record the dropout comparison for each reported loss and condition. The margin-ratio/gap observations are described in text but their numerical values are figure-only; they do not test V7’s magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Other version topics are mentioned as related work, not tested.
record.test_reason: Table 1 directly tests V6 by comparing held-out accuracy with and without dropout in convolutional classifiers. This uses the original intervention and outcome measure. The margin-distribution results do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive a margin-distribution generalization bound and conclude that optimizing their margin-distribution loss controls capacity, learns more separable representations, and improves generalization. Their empirical correlation concerns margin ratio, not measured magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces and trains with a convex margin-distribution loss (mdNet), comparing it with cross-entropy, hinge and soft-hinge losses; it does not reproduce the original interventions in most listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test accuracy varies with dataset, training-set fraction, batch-normalization setting, dropout condition, and loss. The margin-ratio/test-error plots vary across datasets, models and epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate more compact margin distributions with lower test error and report faster decline of the empirical generalization gap with increasing sample size for mdNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin-distribution optimization can improve held-out performance and sample-size scaling of the generalization gap in the tested convolutional classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Networks (accepted manuscript; paper cites Neural Networks, 2022)
record.problems: The reported margin-ratio/generalization-gap trends are mainly shown in figures without recoverable numerical values here. The experiments cover three image datasets and architectures, use validation-based hyperparameter search, and do not test random-label memorization. The dropout table reports ± values but does not define them in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: None. There are 49 rows, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and recovery strategies.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.

Fully connected classifiers; dropout-strength sweeps and excessive-dropout underfitting; the very-small-sample failure regime; joint dropout and weight-decay removal with augmentation. Reduced training fractions alone do not establish the original very-small-sample regime.
Empirical magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All r1–r48 accuracy values and baselines match Table 1, including ImageNet's 5‰ fraction. The paper does not define the ± values or report significance tests, so overlapping uncertainty alone cannot establish absence. Dropout rates and detailed training budgets are unspecified. The study is not an original source for V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

Fully connected classifiers; regimes with very small training sets beyond the paper’s 5% fraction; dropout-strength sweep and explicit evidence of underfitting from excessive dropout; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons against norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: LeNet, AlexNet and ResNet-18 (aggregated in text)
rows.operation_detail: Track empirical generalization gap alongside margin ratio across epochs; numerical points are figure-only.
rows.measure: test error and margin ratio; relation to generalization gap
rows.note: The text says more compact margin distributions get better prediction performance and describes faster generalization-gap convergence for mdNet. This is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
rows.check: Margin ratio is a different construct from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. This aggregates several outcomes and experiments; retain as a finding outside the versions, rather than an observed claim effect.

relationships.condition: LeNet/MNIST and AlexNet/CIFAR-10, full and 5% training sets, with and without batch normalization, across four losses.
relationships.reason: r1–r32 show higher mean test accuracy with dropout in every comparison; gains range from 0.324 to 19.819 percentage points.
relationships.display_finding: Adding dropout raised mean test accuracy in the verified MNIST and CIFAR-10 comparisons; the broader reported pattern remains unverified.
